page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which are allocated from a single shared physical core supporting 2 threads. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2642.19. However, because the physical core is shared, multi-core performance drops significantly, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 10%, which limits data-intensive operations.

Due to its shared-core architecture and low memory bandwidth, the e2-medium is positioned as a highly cost-efficient option for lightweight workloads. It is not suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded processing. Instead, it is best utilized for basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, microservices, and development or testing environments where continuous high CPU utilization is not required.
